drone.rationale: A denied corridor should fail closed rather than extrapolating the low-observable path into unsupported airspace.
High-threat replanning stays unsupported when the mission has no remaining budget for a low-observable reroute.
Critical battery and high threat jointly require a compound policy not present in the registry.
The platform needs an emergency recovery action that is not audited in the finite action set.
Dual comms and navigation loss exceeds the audited single-action router.
Severe weather and threat avoidance conflict with the one-action policy envelope.
Battery preservation, position hold, and descent cues all compete with no single audited action.
Contested airspace and restricted rules should force manual handoff when operator control remains feasible.
High-threat, high-value missions should escalate to manual_handoff when operator takeover is feasible but autonomous recovery is not allowed.

sre.rationale: Failover-ready regional outages remain unsupported when the control plane is unavailable and human escalation is too slow to be feasible.
Readonly is no longer supported once quorum is lost and coordinated intervention is required, but the regional handoff path is still unavailable on service-scoped incidents.
Conflicting service scope, write-path loss, and node-like replica skew should remain unsupported rather than forcing a single audited action.
Lost quorum and unavailable control plane should force a human page when the operator can still respond inside the mitigation window.
A coordinated regional response still pages a human even when the control plane has not fully disappeared.
